claim_being_audited: That certifying the model is policy-compliant if the launch proceeds as a monitored rollout with explicit model-card disclosure of the known small-business onboarding limitation, despite that segment remaining exposed and the current risk-acceptance draft being incomplete.
decision_criteria: If admissible evidence shows the affected use case remains exposed, certification is not supported by rollout controls alone.
If admissible evidence shows explicit pre-launch model-card disclosure of the material limitation for the named launch use case, that would satisfy the disclosure duty described in the policy text.
If a reviewed and applicable risk acceptance exists covering the exposed segment, that could also satisfy the policy predicate.
Absent evidence of either completed disclosure or approved risk acceptance, the certification defense remains incomplete.
evidence_requests: Provide the actual model card or launch disclosure text showing the small-business onboarding limitation is explicitly disclosed for the named launch use case.
Provide the underlying policy document or approval checklist showing whether disclosure alone is sufficient for certification when the affected segment remains exposed.
Provide the launch cohort definition confirming the small-business onboarding segment is in scope for the initial rollout.
Provide the current risk-acceptance record and approval status, including whether any reviewed exception exists for this exposed segment.
Provide the underlying evidence behind the aggregate readiness and rehearsal claims so their relevance to the disclosure decision can be verified.
specific_concerns: Evidence access is limited to the actor's summary, so the cited items cannot be independently checked for wording, scope, or applicability.

The policy text clearly says rollout controls do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed; that undercuts any broader certification rationale based on phased rollout or rollback alone.

The packet says the current risk-acceptance draft is incomplete and does not specifically cover the exposed segment, leaving a required policy predicate unresolved unless disclosure is actually completed before launch.
No admissible evidence is provided showing that the required model-card disclosure has in fact been drafted, reviewed, and attached to the launch decision.
The recommendation is stronger than the proven record: the summary supports a need for disclosure and monitoring, but not the completed compliance state needed to certify.
unsupported_claims: That certification is currently supportable, rather than only conditionally supportable if explicit pre-launch model-card disclosure is completed.
That the cited public guidance materially supports the enterprise policy conclusion, as opposed to providing only general background on monitoring and model-card practices.
Any implication that aggregate readiness, absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents, or rollback capability by themselves satisfy the policy threshold for the exposed use case.
